keyframe_review.note: 1.8 k km2 (six cells at Memel). The Treaties of Tilsit (7 and 9 July 1807) cut Prussia's area from 5,700 to 2,800 square miles (a ratio of 0.49) and its population from 9.75 million to no more than 4.5 million. The land that remained: the 1806 shape without Hanover, Ansbach, Cleves, the Elbe's left bank (Westphalia), the Polish partition lands (Duchy of Warsaw), Danzig and Białystok. This reconstruction is 732 of the 1806 shape's 1,499 cells, a ratio of 0.49.

ledger.note: 5 April 1795: the Peace of Basel gives France the Prussian lands on the left bank of the Rhine. Peace of Basel page: 'The first treaty, on 5 April 1795 between France and Prussia, had been under discussion since 1794'; 'In secret, Prussia recognised the French control of the west bank of the Rhine pending a cession by the Imperial Diet'. War of the First Coalition page: the war 'cost Prussia its territories on the left bank of the Rhine'; the Peace of Basel 'recognized France's occupation of the left bank of the Rhine'. Neither page names Cleves, Moers or Upper Guelders: the land is my reading (the 12 cells of Cliopatria's 1791 shape west of the Rhine, 3,000 km2; the German mediatisation page's table gives Prussia's losses in the 1803 settlement as 2,000 km2 and 140,000 people without naming the lands). Cliopatria's 1794 shape already omits 10 of the 12 cells (it dates the French occupation to 1794; the pages read give no year for it) and keeps 2 until the 1805 shape, which the keyframes remove. The cession was formal only later (Lunéville, 1801; the Final Recess of 25 February 1803). Repair 2026-10-25.

wars.name: Great Northern War (Prussia's part)

zones.text: half of Swedish Pomerania (the Kingdom of Prussia page: all of it east of the River Oder); the 14 cells Cliopatria adds to its 1713 shape on the Pomeranian coast (13 in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and one on Usedom)

wars.outcome: Prussia kept its conquest: the Treaty of Stockholm (21 January 1720) gave it Western Pomerania south of the Peene with Stettin and the islands of Wolin and Usedom; Sweden kept the rest, which Denmark returned on 17 January 1721.
wars.note: The page puts the war in Pomerania in 1714-1716 (Charles XII at Stralsund from November 1714 to December 1715; Denmark in Rügen and north of the Peene) and gives no year for Prussia's taking; it does not mention a 1713 sequestration of Stettin. The start year 1715 is a bridge (ledger occupation, confidence 1). Added 2026-10-25 (reviewer eu-09-k).

wars.name: First Silesian War
wars.outcome: Prussian victory: the Treaty of Breslau (11 June 1742) gave Prussia most of Silesia and the County of Glatz, 35,000 km2 and about a million subjects.
wars.note: The page says the treaty was 'later formalised in the Treaty of Berlin' without a date; the History of Prussia page has Lower Silesia taken after Mollwitz on 10 April 1741 and Upper Silesia in 1742.

wars.name: Second Silesian War

zones.text: Bohemia, held from 15 August to November 1744

wars.outcome: Prussia invaded Bohemia on 15 August 1744, took Prague on 16 September and fell back into Upper Silesia in November; the Treaty of Dresden (25 December 1745) left Silesia with Prussia, and Maria Theresa acknowledged Prussian control of Glatz there. The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) left Prussia 'in possession of most of Silesia'.

wars.name: Third Silesian War (Seven Years' War in Europe)

zones.text: East Prussia, invaded by the Russians in 1757 (Gross-Jägersdorf, 30 August 1757)
Bohemia, invaded by Frederick II on 18 April 1757 (the Battle of Prague, 6 May 1757; Kolín followed)
the County of Glatz (Kłodzko), captured by the Austrians under Laudon in 1760 and returned to Prussia in 1763; the gazetteer lacks the name
Pomerania, invaded by Sweden with 17,000 men (1757) until the truce of Peter III's government (1762)
Prussia's Rhineland territories (Cleves and the Lower Rhine, Mark and Westphalia: the 23 cells Cliopatria drops from 1757), held by France until the peace of 1762-1763

wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum: the Treaty of Hubertusburg (February 1763) confirmed Prussia's control of Silesia; Russia had made peace at Saint Petersburg on 5 May 1762.
wars.note: The page puts the 'Miracle of the House of Brandenburg' after Kunersdorf (12 August 1759) and records the Russian and Austrian occupation of Berlin in late 1760. Repair 2026-10-25, from the Seven Years' War page: Prussia entered Bohemia on 18 April 1757 and won at Prague on 6 May 1757 (Kolín is undated there, Breslau not mentioned); the Austrians took Glatz in 1760 and it was 'returned to Prussia in exchange for the Prussian evacuation of Saxony' in 1763; Sweden invaded Pomerania; East Prussia was 'occupied by Russian forces over the winter and would remain under their control until 1762'; Berlin was briefly occupied in October 1760; Louis XV 'evacuated Prussia's Rhineland territories' (Cleves and Wesel are not named, and no start year is given). The zones are war zones only: no ledger event dates the Bohemian, Glatz or Rhenish phases.

wars.name: War of the First Coalition (Prussia's part)

zones.text: Prussia's lands on the left bank of the Rhine (Cleves west of the Rhine, Moers, Upper Guelders): the 12 cells of Cliopatria's 1791 shape west of the Rhine between 51.3 and 52.1 N

wars.outcome: Prussia declared war in June 1792, invaded France with the Duke of Brunswick's army, retreated after Valmy (20 September 1792) and made the Peace of Basel on 5 April 1795, which recognised France's occupation of the left bank of the Rhine and cost Prussia its territories there.
wars.note: The page names no Prussian place on the left bank and dates neither Fleurus nor the occupation; Cliopatria drops the cells in 1794. The Second and Third Partitions of Poland (23 January 1793, 24 October 1795) run alongside and are in the ledger. Added 2026-10-25 (reviewer eu-09-k).

wars.name: War of the Fourth Coalition (Prussia's part)
wars.outcome: Prussia defeated at Jena-Auerstedt on 14 October 1806; the Treaties of Tilsit (7 and 9 July 1807) halved its area (5,700 to 2,800 square miles) and population (9.75 to no more than 4.5 million), with an indemnity set at 154.5 million francs on 9 March 1808 and an army limit of 43,000.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Prussia page says about half of the territory; the History of Prussia page says about one-third. The Tilsit page's own figures give 0.49.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition (Prussia's part)

zones.text: Saxony, where Lützen (2 May 1813), Bautzen (20-21 May) and Leipzig (16-19 October) were fought

wars.outcome: Prussia changed sides (Treaty of Kalisch, 28 February 1813; declaration of war 13 March, received in Paris 16 March) and the war ended with the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814; the Prussian king entered Paris with the coalition armies on 31 March 1814.
wars.note: The page does not describe the reoccupation of Prussia's lost lands or the crossing of the Rhine, so keyframe 1814 stays unverified; the restoration is dated by the Final Act of 9 June 1815 (ledger). Added 2026-10-25 (reviewer eu-09-k).

wars.name: War of the Seventh Coalition (Prussia's part)
wars.outcome: The war lasted 20 March to 8 July 1815: Blücher's Prussians lost at Ligny (16 June) and arrived at Waterloo (18 June) 'with the aid of several Prussian corps'; the Second Treaty of Paris (20 November 1815) ended the Napoleonic Wars and France was reduced to its 1790 boundaries.
wars.note: The page names no territorial change for Prussia (Saarbrücken and Saarlouis are not mentioned), so the zones are empty. Added 2026-10-25 (reviewer eu-09-k).

wars.name: First Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum: Prussian troops crossed the Dannevirke into Schleswig on 19 April 1848 and took Fredericia on 2 May; Prussia signed the Armistice of Malmö on 26 August 1848 and made peace with Denmark by the Treaty of Berlin on 2 July 1850; the London Protocol of 1852 settled it.
wars.note: The page dates the war 24 March 1848 to 8 May 1852; the years here are Prussia's part (to the Treaty of Berlin). No border changed, so the ledger has no event. kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 lists the war 1848-1852. Added 2026-10-25 (reviewer eu-09-k).

wars.name: Second Schleswig War

union.text: the Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg (Ratzeburg, Mölln, Lauenburg); the gazetteer lacks the name

wars.outcome: Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria (Treaty of Vienna, 30 October 1864); the Gastein Convention of 14 August 1865 gave Prussia the administration of Schleswig and Austria that of Holstein, and the Prussian king took Lauenburg in personal union in September 1865.
wars.note: The war began on 1 February 1864 (Second Schleswig War page). Repair 2026-10-25: source changed from the History of Prussia page to the war's own article, which the original run had not opened; the Gastein day is on that page and on the Austro-Prussian War page.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussian victory: armistice 22 July (preliminary peace at Nikolsburg 26 July), the Peace of Prague on 23 August 1866 dissolved the German Confederation, excluded Austria from German affairs and let Prussia annex Hanover, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau, Frankfurt and Schleswig-Holstein.
wars.note: Bavaria lost Bad Orb, Gersfeld and the Kaulsdorf exclave; Saxony was spared and joined the North German Confederation the next year.

certainty.note: Treaty frontiers: Breslau 1742, Hubertusburg 1763, the partition treaties 1772, 1793, 1795. Wartime occupations (Saxony 1756-1763, the Russian advances 1758-1762) are soft, as are the scattered Rhenish and Franconian lands as drawn from Cliopatria.
The Tilsit rump and the French occupation (to 1812): the frontier is drawn from a reconstruction, not from a surveyed line.
The Final Act of 9 June 1815 and the Peace of Prague (1866) fix the frontiers; the Neuchâtel and Hohenzollern exclaves are approximate.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 from the nine pages in sources (the page budget for 28 shapes). Repaired the same day after reviewer eu-09-k failed it: twelve further pages were opened for the findings and the thin items (22 sources in all, well over the 9-page budget, because the reviewer asked for them); the repair log is the last paragraph.

End of the state. The Kingdom of Prussia page dates the kingdom 1701-1918 and the Free State to 9 November 1918 ('Prussia as a whole was abolished in 1947'). This dossier ends on 1 July 1867 because Cliopatria draws the North German Confederation (1868-1870) and the German Empire (1871-) as separate states on the same land; Cliopatria's own Kingdom of Prussia row stops at 1863. If the colour agent prefers one colour for Prussia to 1918, extend the end and drop the merge; the successor handover (Confederation, then Empire) is recorded in identity.successors.

Cliopatria rows that are Prussia under other names. Its Kingdom of Prussia shapes from 1807 are slivers (1.8 k km2 at Memel in 1807-1808; 87 km2, one cell in the Netherlands, in 1814; 594 km2 at Neuchâtel in 1815-1833; 1,067 km2 in 1834-1847; 473 km2 in Mecklenburg in 1863) and the real Prussia of 1809-1866 is drawn in other rows: Confederation of the Rhine 1809-1813 (170.6 k km2: the Tilsit rump, plus Swedish Pomerania), German Confederation 1815-1865 (281.7 k km2 in 1820: exactly Prussia's provinces, none of Bavaria, Hanover, Württemberg or the rest of Saxony), North German Confederation 1868-1870 (365 k km2). The 1815-1819 German Confederation shape (342.9 k km2) adds Hanover and Saxony. This dossier takes 1820's shape (and 1840, 1846, 1853, 1863 for the later years) as Prussia's land. The German Confederation (eu-20) and Confederation of the Rhine dossiers must therefore not also paint the same cells as their own territory: they are associations of states (umbrella), and the cells belong to Prussia. The orchestrator should reconcile.

Corrections that rest on Cliopatria alone. The 1815-1863 corrections use German Confederation shapes; the 1807-1814 'rump' is the 1806 shape without the lands Tilsit named (Hanover, Ansbach, the Elbe's left bank, the Duchy of Warsaw, Danzig, Białystok): 732 of 1499 cells, a ratio of 0.49 against the Tilsit page's 2,800 / 5,700 square miles (0.49).
